title: Immutability and Value-Oriented Design
subtopics: Trade-offs in mutable and immutable models
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of immutability and value-oriented design and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—immutable classes—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study immutability and value-oriented design with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you keep a Java codebase understandable as its responsibilities and collaborators grow. In this lesson, focus on immutable classes and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Encapsulation protects invariants by keeping mutable state private and validating updates through a small public API. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect immutable classes with defensive copying before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Prefer immutable value-oriented models where identity and ongoing mutation are not required. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
